text:
alex: Ran a focused nsys+perfetto capture on the 8xA100 TP run — seeing repeating ~1.2ms gaps between tensor-parallel matmul kernels that line up with NCCL AllReduce starts. uploading traces: https://perfetto.local/r/abcd1234 :mag: 

alex: Command I used:

```sh
nsys profile -o tp_run --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=none 
  ./run_inference.sh --model=redwood-v1 --tp=8 --batch_size=16
```

alex: In the timeline you can see a pattern: large matmul -> small memcpy -> NCCL_Allreduce kickoff -> idle gap -> smaller matmul kernel. The kernel_selector seems to intermittently pick a smaller FP16 fallback kernel for certain sequence lengths, causing more kernel launches and higher per-launch overhead.

maria: can you dump the kernel names + durations? curious if the smaller kernels are the quantized path or a fallback. also any KV-cache churn around those times? :thinking_face: 

alex: quick snippet from the nsys summary (trimmed):

```csv
kernel_name,duration_us,sm_eff,launches
matmul_q8_ker,780,88,118
matmul_fp16_fast,1180,93,47
matmul_fp16_slow,420,61,336
nccl_allreduce,900,na,24
```

alex: note matmul_fp16_slow has many launches but low SM efficiency -> suggests micro-batching or tiny sequence fragments.

cheng: that matches a batching-heuristic edge case we saw. If KV cache hit rate drops below the heuristic threshold we shrink the local micro-batch and end up hitting the slower kernel family. check runtime config: `batch_threshold=0.6` and `continuous_batch_window_ms=8` — both can force earlier kernel dispatch.

alex: good call. I also see in the NVTX trace KV retire spikes ~2.3ms right before the NCCL peaks. Could be KV handshake forcing synchronization.

nsight-bot: NCCL trace attached (nccl_trace_1754.nct). AllReduce start times show 3 distinct hotspots repeating every 60ms.

maria: infra-bot, did we roll the kernel-selector tweak last week? I remember a PR that tried to bias toward smaller kernels for latency at small batch sizes.

infra-bot: candidate rollout 2026-02-10 included change `kernel_selector: prefer_smaller_kernels=true` from PR #4123.

maria: ok that explains it. For models with TP and high KV churn that heuristic backfires. Two options: revert the selector change in canary for TP workloads, or add a rule to prefer larger kernels when `tp_sharded=true`. Quick mitigation: runtime override `kernel_selection=prefer_large_kernels` or pin `KERNEL_PIN=matmul_q8_ker`.

cheng: also try bumping `continuous_batch_window_ms` to 16 to give the dispatcher more time to group sequences into the larger kernel. we saw similar when debugging batch splay. run with:

```env
RK_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=16 KERNEL_PIN=matmul_q8_ker ./run_inference.sh ...
```

alex: will run that in a canary with the selector flag off. Plan: 1) run 1k inferences with RK_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=16 + KERNEL_PIN=matmul_q8_ker, 2) capture nsys + perfetto, 3) compare allreduce overlap and idle gaps.

maria: sounds good. if you get <50% of previous allreduce stalls we can push a targeted rollback for TP models. :thumbsup: 

alex: update after 200 inferences on canary — visible improvement: ~40% reduction in the 1.2ms idle gaps and NCCL peaks are narrower. Re-running extended trace now, will link perfetto when ready.

cheng: nice. can you also collect `cupti_activity` for kernel launch latencies? helps show per-launch overhead vs compute time.

alex: yes — next run includes CUPTI sampling. posting full perfetto link when upload finishes. thanks all.
